title: Kyrgyzstan approves crypto framework, liquidates KGST issuer on September 5
dek: Kyrgyzstan's government approved a cryptocurrency regulatory framework and dual stablecoin strategy on September 5, 2026, while simultaneously liquidating OAJ 'ElPay', the entity that issued the som-pegged KGST stablecoin. The framework includes licensing requirements, banking integration, and a new analytics platform for compliance monitoring.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: The National Council for the Development of Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies, chaired by President Sadyr Japarov, approved the framework while ordering liquidation of KGST's issuer despite the stablecoin's December 2025 listing on Binance.
bottom_line: The liquidation of KGST's issuer while approving a stablecoin framework raises questions about continuity of both initiatives. Whether Kyrgyzstan's banking channels for crypto operations and analytics platform launch on schedule, and whether KGST survives the shutdown of its issuer, will indicate whether this framework can function as written.
body: Kyrgyzstan's National Council for the Development of Virtual Assets and Blockchain Technologies convened on September 5, 2026, chaired by President Sadyr Japarov, to approve a comprehensive cryptocurrency regulatory framework. The meeting carried a central contradiction: the council approved liquidation of OAJ 'ElPay', the entity that issued KGST, the som-pegged stablecoin that had become the first from the Commonwealth of Independent States region to land a Binance listing in December 2025.

The framework establishes a dual stablecoin strategy. KGST was designed for domestic transactions and som-denominated commerce; USDKG, a gold-backed stablecoin pegged to the US dollar and issued by a state-controlled entity, targets cross-border payments and international trade. USDKG was registered on October 31, 2025, with an initial issuance of approximately $50 million. Both stablecoins are required to be fully collateralized and registered with reserves held in licensed banks under the current regulatory framework.

The government's stated goals for both stablecoins include enhancing financial inclusion, facilitating domestic transactions, and enabling cheaper cross-border payments. The framework also addresses the establishment of local banking channels for crypto operations and includes discussion of a new cryptocurrency analytics platform intended to help authorities monitor transactions and enforce sanctions requirements.

Kyrgyzstan's legal foundation for crypto regulation dates to the 2022 Law on Virtual Assets, amended multiple times through 2025 and 2026. The $50 million USDKG issuance represents a meaningful commitment of state resources for a country with GDP under $12 billion. Former Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao has been serving as a presidential adviser on digital assets since 2025.

The liquidation of ElPay presents a tension in the framework's execution. Over 25 entities associated with the Kyrgyz digital asset sector currently face sanctions, signaling endemic compliance and enforcement risk across the ecosystem. The regulatory framework's requirement for banking integration and licensed custody creates dependency on traditional finance channels that may prove restrictive. The timing and reasoning behind ElPay's liquidation, and whether KGST continues to exist post-shutdown, remain unaddressed in available reporting.
